PullRequest.Title: automations: wait for manual run session identity resolution
PullRequest.Body:

## Code stats
- **Total diff:** +103/-2 against `main` at `c542a8375bbb24fb0020f7b03c800f74a8cea7e2`.
- **Implementation:** +10/-2.
- **Tests:** +93/-0, 8 added, 320 passed.
- **Split:** 11.4% implementation, 88.6% tests.
- **Changed-line coverage:** not measured.
- **Where the change lives:**
  - `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts`: +93/-0 (88.6%).
  - `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/agentHostAutomationStore.ts`: +10/-2 (11.4%).

## Summary
Fix a false manual automation error: "The Agent Host ended the run without a session."

The host can publish an automation run's `primarySession` before its provisional session is advertised to the client. With provider-neutral session URIs, the client cannot project that resource until discovery supplies its identity. Run Now previously returned too early and reported a missing session even though the run was still running and later completed successfully.

Wait for client session identity resolution and recheck when it changes. Preserve cancellation and real sessionless terminal outcomes. If a linked run finishes before discovery arrives, bound the remaining identity wait with the existing 30-second observation timeout. Scheduling and host execution are unchanged.

Related regression candidate: #339492. No separate issue was supplied for this report.

## Validation
- `npm run compile` - passed (full client/extensions/Copilot compilation).
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\browser\agentHostAutomationStore.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- The following targeted suites passed: **320 tests**.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat `
  --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts `
  --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\automationRunner.test.ts `
  --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\providerAutomationService.test.ts `
  --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\automations\test\browser\automationTools.test.ts `
  --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\automationsView.test.ts `
  --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostAutomationService.test.ts `
  --reporter dot
```

New tests cover delayed identity for standard and opaque host URIs, completion before discovery, cancellation, disconnection, catalogue errors, timeout, and listener cleanup. The delayed-identity regression cases failed before the implementation change.

**Live Windows Code OSS verification:** three recorded manual Run Now attempts all returned "Hello world!" without the false error; a real 09:45 scheduled run also succeeded without the error. Host lifecycle logs independently confirm all four completed successfully. Recordings and screenshots are retained in the working session. The test automation was restored to Manual.

Independent Astra and Opus reviews reported no concrete introduced bugs.

Copilot code review reviewed `155650d326f` and recommended approval with **0 findings**. The requested ten-minute review wait was completed; no follow-up code changes or re-review were needed.

Not run: full repository test suite, live remote-host validation, or cross-platform UI runs. No claim of exhaustive regression absence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manual Run Now where the Agent Host publishes a primary session before that backend identity is advertised to the client
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing runAutomation host request must return and the authoritative automation catalogue must contain the run; after the diff, client progress additionally waits for the in-memory session-resolution mapping or a terminal state. Session projection is required before AutomationRunner can complete whenDispatched with a usable session resource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one manual automation run request to the local or remote Agent Host and receive catalogue updates through the existing subscription
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one runAutomation request per accepted manual dispatch; catalogue updates are subscription events rather than per-run polling calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single host request and catalogue subscription were used; the client returned as soon as primarySession was present or the run was terminal, without waiting for the local identity mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The host request and first qualifying catalogue/session-resolution update must complete before the dispatch result is exposed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each resolution event checks the catalogue until it finds the requested run. The host initially exposes at most 50 terminal runs per automation plus active runs, though explicitly fetched history can enlarge the catalogue; effective pending-listener cardinality is the number of concurrently unresolved manual runs across distinct automations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active run is permitted per automation by getActiveRunFor; different automations can run concurrently. Each unresolved manual dispatch owns one catalogue listener and one session-resolution listener, with no added subprocess or boundary concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm _backendSessions identity mapping makes hasResolvedSession succeed immediately. A cold miss waits for onDidChangeSessionResolution; registration fires that event, and there is no boundary retry or negative-cache loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new wait and local scans are on the manual-dispatch critical path; high confidence that sessionResource resolution is an in-memory lookup and that the existing host request count remains one.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A very large explicitly expanded catalogue or many simultaneously unresolved runs could increase synchronous predicate scans, but manual dispatch concurrency and session-advertisement event frequency are normally low, and the diff adds no expensive boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added latency is the intentional identity-resolution gate needed to avoid returning an unusable session, and the incremental work is bounded local event handling rather than new I/O or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: The run reaches a terminal state before its advertised session identity becomes resolvable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first wait ends at terminal state, then the second local wait allows late session discovery for up to the existing 30-second mutation timeout. If identity arrives, dispatch completes; otherwise the timeout surfaces the existing failure path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe terminal automation state over the already-open Agent Host catalogue subscription
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional request is sent; one existing subscription update marks the run terminal, followed only by local event observation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The client consumed the same terminal catalogue update and returned immediately, potentially producing a false sessionless error before identity discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Terminal catalogue delivery starts the bounded identity-resolution grace period; no new boundary operation blocks it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is one retained local wait per terminal unresolved dispatch for at most 30 seconds; predicate work scales with catalogue entries/runs on catalogue or session-resolution events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One timeout and one catalogue/session-resolution listener set per unresolved terminal manual dispatch. Different automations may overlap, but there is no spawned work, polling, or added remote concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A mapping already present at terminal transition resolves synchronously. A late positive registration wakes the wait. An unresolved miss is not cached and is bounded by the 30-second timeout after terminal state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the timeout, listener lifecycle, and absence of added boundary calls based on _waitForCatalog and the new tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact incidence and delay of lost or late discovery are unknown; the test explicitly establishes the 30-second upper bound and listener cleanup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue. The bounded post-terminal wait is an explicit correctness tradeoff, cleans up on every settlement path, and does not retain resources beyond the timeout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manual Run Now is cancelled, the provider disconnects, or the catalogue errors while identity resolution is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancellation fires the combined local event and forwards the existing host cancellation action when supported; disconnect disposes the connection-scoped store; catalogue errors reject the wait. These paths terminate the identity wait without requiring session discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally send one AutomationRunCancelRequested action to the Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cancellation action per manual run, deduplicated by cancellationForwarded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cancellation forwarding and connection/catalogue disposal already existed; the diff adds cancellation as a wake-up event for the identity predicates but does not add another boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cancellation can unblock the new local wait and proceeds over the same connection; disconnect/error paths complete locally through disposal or subscription error.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resource usage scales linearly with concurrently pending manual dispatches, with one DisposableStore and a small fixed listener set per dispatch until settlement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation dispatch remains at most once due cancellationForwarded. Store disposal clears all pending waits together; no retry queue or burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session cache state is irrelevant once cancellation, disconnect, or catalogue error wins; no stale or negative cache entry is retained by the changed code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because _pendingWaits owns and disposes every listener store, and added tests assert listener cleanup for all these outcomes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent manual runs across many distinct automations are possible but no realistic high-cardinality trigger was established in the reviewed call path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cleanup remains deterministic and the diff does not amplify cancellation I/O or retain unresolved listeners after settlement.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced manual automation dispatch through AutomationRunner, provider stores, local/remote Agent Host boundaries, catalogue history limits, session identity registration, cancellation, timeout, and disposal. The PR adds event-driven local waiting and catalogue scans but no new IPC/network/filesystem operation, polling, concurrency burst, or unbounded retained cache. No valid performance finding was identified.
